blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Mixture-of-experts (MoE) routers typically apply softmax to the router scores and keep the top- K K experts, making every token use exactly K K experts.
Sparsity-inducing probability maps such as sparsemax, α \alpha -entmax and normmax can adaptively assign exact zeros to selected experts, and therefore appear to offer token-dependent expert participation, even when using the same top- K K machinery.
In this work, we study whether and how this sparsity survives training.
We train matched 300M and 1B top-2 MoE language models with softmax, 1.5 1.5 -entmax, sparsemax and 2 2 -normmax, and find that the maps behave very differently once trained: at 1B, entmax discards 30% less probability mass than softmax while almost never dropping a selected expert, sparsemax retains the most mass, and normmax routes 21% of tokens to a single expert.
These outcomes are not properties of the maps alone.
Each map drops a selected expert only when the gap between the two largest scores reaches a fixed threshold, and the trained routers differ in the score distribution they learn: the entmax router learns scores with roughly half the spread of softmax’s, which keeps its top-2 gaps below its threshold, while sparsemax and normmax, which share the same threshold, learn different gap distributions and hence different participation.
Routers thus co-adapt their scores to the map, and a map’s capacity to produce zeros does not by itself determine expert participation.
While none of the sparse maps improves validation loss over softmax, they make the trained models far less sensitive to selecting more experts at inference: sparsemax trained with K = 2 K{=}2 loses 0.02 0.02 nats when run with K = 8 K{=}8 , where softmax loses 0.58 0.58 .
Our results indicate that adaptive MoE routing has to be designed around the joint behavior of the probability map and the learned scores, rather than around the map alone. 1 1 1 Our code will be released upon acceptance.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers scale model capacity by activating only a few expert networks per token ( Shazeer et al., 2017 ; Fedus et al., 2022 ; Jiang et al., 2024 ) .
A router scores the experts, a probability map turns the scores into weights, and a top- K K operator keeps the K K highest-weighted experts, whose outputs are combined with the renormalized weights.
With softmax, every token uses exactly K K experts, regardless of how many it needs, and the selected experts often account for only a fraction of the router’s probability mass—the rest is discarded by truncation.

一个路由器给专家打分,一个概率图把分数转换为权重,一个上-K接线员保留着KK最高权重的专家,其输出与再正态权重结合.
每个信使使用K K 专家, 不论需要多少人, 被选中的专家往往只占路由器概率质量的一小部分, 其余的则被截取而去。

blocks.en:
Sparsity-inducing probability maps promise a way out without changing the top- K K machinery.
Sparsemax ( Martins and Astudillo, 2016 ) , α \alpha -entmax ( Peters et al., 2019 ) and normmax ( Santos et al., 2024 ; Santos et al., 2025 ) can assign exact zeros , so a selected expert may receive zero weight and drop out of the mixture.
The number of experts that actually contribute to a token is then data-dependent , even when the expert budget K K stays fixed.
Several recent routers also build on this idea ( Oldfield et al., 2024 ; Thaman, 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) .
However, how sparsity behaves in these models is not obvious.
Since the router scores are learned, changing the map also changes the scores that the map receives: a trained sparsemax router and a trained softmax router differ both in how they transform scores and in which scores they learned to produce.
As a result, a map that can produce zeros may rarely do so once its router has been trained

blocks.en:
In this paper, we study whether the sparsity of the probability map survives training, and what determines expert participation when it does not.
We train matched 300M and 1B top-2 MoE language models with softmax, 1.5 1.5 -entmax, sparsemax and 2 2 -normmax under an identical architecture, data and balancing objective, and we measure the probability mass retained by the selected experts ( retention ), the number of selected experts with non-zero weight ( participation ), and predictive quality.
To relate the map to the scores it receives, we record the router scores of every trained model and measure how their spread and top-2 gaps sit relative to each map’s sparsification threshold.
Figure 1 summarizes the setting and the outcomes.
We find that a map’s ability to produce zeros does not, by itself, determine how many experts a token uses.
Our main contributions are: • A controlled study of sparse maps as MoE routers. We train top-2 MoE language models at two scales that differ only in the probability map, and measure retention, participation, load balance and predictive quality, together with the router scores of every trained model (§ 3 ). • Retention and participation are distinct outcomes. Under top-2 selection, mass is discarded only when more than two experts have positive probability, while participation drops only when a single expert does (Equation 7 ). The trained routers land in different regimes: at 1B, 1.5 1.5 -entmax discards 30 % 30\% less mass than softmax yet keeps both experts for 99.95 % 99.95\% of tokens, whereas normmax-2 routes 21 % 21\% of tokens to a single expert (§ 4.2 ). • The map’s threshold and the learned scores jointly set participation. Each map drops a selected expert exactly when the top-2 gap reaches a fixed threshold. The sparse routers learn smaller score spreads than softmax, keeping 1.5 1.5 -entmax’s gaps below its threshold of 2 2 ; sparsemax and normmax-2 share the threshold 1 1 , yet route 6.9 % 6.9\% and 21.3 % 21.3\% of tokens to one expert, as their routers learn different gap distributions (§ 4.3 ). • Sparse maps reduce sensitivity to the inference-time budget. None improves validation loss at the trained budget, but running the 1B models trained with K = 2 K{=}2 at K = 8 K{=}8 costs sparsemax 0.02 0.02 nats against 0.58 0.58 for softmax, as sparsemax gives zero weight to most of the extra slots (§ 4.4 ).

blocks.zh: 3 实验设置

blocks.en:
We train MoE language models at two scales with a Llama 3-style backbone ( Grattafiori et al., 2024 ) in which every second feed-forward block is replaced by an MoE layer: a 300M model (8 layers, width 320, 4 MoE layers with 26 experts each) and a 1B model (9 layers, width 768, 4 MoE layers with 27 experts each).
Every token selects K = 2 K=2 experts, following Mixtral’s selection and weighted combination ( Jiang et al., 2024 ) , without capacity constraints or token dropping; the 1B model has 302 302 M active parameters.
The four maps share everything except π \pi , including the balancing objective of Equation ( 5 ) with coefficient 0.01 0.01 , averaged over MoE layers and evaluated on local microbatches.
A dense model of matching depth and width at each scale provides a reference with a larger active-parameter budget.
All models are trained on DCLM-baseline ( Li et al., 2024 ) for 10 10 B tokens ( 19,073 19{,}073 updates of 524,288 524{,}288 tokens) with AdamW, cosine decay and bfloat16 mixed precision. Appendices A.1 and A.2 give the architecture details and the full training and evaluation recipe.

blocks.en:
We first check that the MoEs are competent models (§ 4.1 ), then ask whether the sparsity of the map survives training (§ 4.2 ), whether the differences between trained routers come from the map or from the scores learned under it (§ 4.3 ), and what the sparse maps buy at inference time (§ 4.4 ).
We report both scales and focus the discussion on the 1B models. The 300M models show the same qualitative routing patterns, with their training curves and load statistics in Appendix C.4 .

Entmax sits almost entirely in the first regime: 99.9 % 99.9\% of its states have s ≥ 3 s\geq 3 , so it retains more mass than softmax while keeping both experts.

4.3 Is it the map, or the scores learned under it?

The trained models differ both in the map and in the scores that the map receives, and the two are easy to separate because each map has a fixed sparsification threshold (see § 2.1 ). Concretely, a selected expert is dropped exactly when the top-2 score gap is at least 2 2 for 1.5 1.5 -entmax and at least 1 1 for sparsemax and normmax-2.
The singleton rate of a trained model is therefore nothing but the fraction of its learned gaps that reach its map’s threshold.
Figure 3 shows these gap distributions for the 1B models, with both thresholds marked in every panel.
The numerical spreads and quantiles at both scales are retained in Table 7 in Appendix C.2 .

Because it uses the full distribution, an expert with zero probability receives no direct balancing gradient under a sparse map, and changing the score scale also changes the probabilities seen by this objective.

blocks.en: 5 Related work
blocks.zh: 5 相关工作

blocks.en:
Softmax followed by top- K K remains the dominant router ( Shazeer et al., 2017 ; Fedus et al., 2022 ; Jiang et al., 2024 ) , with sigmoid scores renormalized among the selected experts as the main production alternative ( DeepSeek-AI, 2024 ) .
Sparse probability maps have been used as routers before. For example, Multilinear MoE compares entmax with softmax over factorized experts ( Oldfield et al., 2024 ) , DUAL studies sparsemax under routing constraints ( Thaman, 2025 ) , and ReMoE replaces the map by rectified gates with a separate sparsity controller ( Wang et al., 2025 ) .
Differentiable relaxations of the selection step itself include DSelect-k, a smooth gate with explicit cardinality control ( Hazimeh et al., 2021 ) , the sparse top- k k operators of Sander et al. (2023) , Soft MoE, which replaces discrete routing by soft slot assignment ( Puigcerver et al., 2024 ) , and, more recently, SoftMoE, a truncated LapSum relaxation with learned per-layer budgets ( Zasada et al., 2026 ) , and ProbMoE, which samples cardinality-constrained subsets and differentiates through inclusion marginals ( Zhao et al., 2026 ) .
These works propose new routers and evaluate them end-to-end, whereas we keep the router fixed to top-2 and ask what a sparse map delivers once the router has been trained with it, and how the score distribution it learns interacts with the map’s sparsification threshold (§ 4.3 ).
blocks.zh:
Softmax后接上-K仍然是主要的路由器(Shazeer等,2017;Fedus等,2022;Jiang等,2024;),所选专家中以sigmoid分数为主要生产替代(DeepSeek-AI,2024.
Sparse概率图在之前就被用作路由器. 例如,多线性MOE将entmax与软max比作因子化专家(Oldfield等,2024年),DUAL在路由限制下研究稀有max(Thaman,2025年),而ReMoE则用单独的螺旋管控制器来修正门来取而代之(Wang等,2025年).
对选择步骤本身的可区分的放松包括:DSelect-k,一个具有明确核心控制的平滑门(Hazimeh等人,2021年),Sander等人(2023年)上下-k的操作者稀少;Soft MoE,它用软槽分配取代了离散的路由(Puigcerver等人,2024年),以及最近SoftMoE, 以每个层次的学习预算(Zasada等人,2026年)来缩短了LapSum的放松;ProbMoE,它通过包容边际(Zhao等人,2026年)来取样主要受约束的子集并区分。
这些作品提出了新的路由器并评价其端到端,而我们则将路由器固定在上到上到下,并询问一旦路由器经过了培训,一个稀疏的地图会提供什么,以及它所学得的分数分配如何与地图的溅射阈值相互作用(第4.3节).

blocks.en:
Balancing objectives range from the Switch-style loss we use ( Fedus et al., 2022 ) to balanced assignment ( Lewis et al., 2021 ; Zhou et al., 2022 ) , loss-free bias adjustment ( Wang et al., 2024 ) and ϕ \phi -Balancing, which targets population-level balance through a convex potential and mirror descent ( Chen et al., 2026 ) . Yoon et al. (2026) show that the task gradient reaches only the selected experts and that balancing provides no token-level counterfactual signal, and Huu et al. (2026) analyze the switching surfaces of top- K K routing and propose smoothing near them.
Our observation that the balancing objective interacts with the map through the full distribution (§ 4.4 ) is complementary: it concerns which experts the balancing gradient can reach under a sparse map.

平衡目标从我们使用的Switch式损失(Fedus等,2022年)到平衡分配(Lewis等,2021年;周等等,2022年),无损失偏差调整(Wang等,2024年)和\\-phi-Balance,通过对流潜力和镜倒取景(Chen等,2026年)以人口水平平衡为目标. Yoon等 (2026年) 显示任务梯度只到达被选中的专家,平衡不提供符号级的反事实信号,而Huu等 (2026年) 分析上-K K出行道的切换表面,并提议在它们附近平滑.
我们的意见是,平衡目标通过充分分布与地图相互作用(第4.4节)是相辅相成的:它涉及的是平衡梯度在稀有地图下可以达到的专家。

blocks.en:
Sparsemax ( Martins and Astudillo, 2016 ) and α \alpha -entmax ( Peters et al., 2019 ) are regularized argmax maps in the Fenchel–Young framework of Blondel et al. (2020) , which also covers the norm entropies behind normmax ( Santos et al., 2024 ; Santos et al., 2025 ) .
Their sparsity has been exploited in attention, where the support size is known to depend on the scale of the scores: Correia et al. (2019) learn α \alpha per head, and Vasylenko et al. (2026) learn a temperature so that α \alpha -entmax attention interpolates between sparse and dense regimes as the context grows.
Our results transfer this observation to routing, where the score scale learned by the router, together with the map’s threshold, sets participation. This suggests that learned scales or shapes are the right knob for adaptive MoE routing.

他们的筋挛被人们所注意的所利用,在那里,支持的大小已知取决于分数的分数: Correia等 (2019年) 学习α-alpha per head,和 Vasylenko等. (2026年)学习温度,使得α-entmax的注意力随着上下文的增长而介于稀疏和密集的制度之间.
我们的结果将这一观察转移到了路由,路由器所学得的分数尺度以及地图的门槛设定了参与度。 这表明所学到的尺度或形状是适应性教育部路线的正确取道.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusions
blocks.zh: 6. 结论

blocks.en:
We studied whether the sparsity of a probability map survives training in a top-2 MoE router.
Across matched 300M and 1B models, the answer is that it survives only partly, and never as a property of the map alone.
The 1.5 1.5 -entmax router retains more probability mass than softmax while keeping both selected experts, the sparsemax router retains the most mass, and the normmax-2 router uses the fewest contributors.
These behaviors are set jointly by the map’s sparsification threshold and by the score distribution the router learns under it.
The 1.5 1.5 -entmax router keeps both experts because its learned scores have half the spread of softmax’s, which keeps its top-2 gaps below the threshold, whereas sparsemax and normmax-2, which sparsify at the same gap, differ only because their routers learned different gap distributions.
Retention, participation and predictive quality also turn out to be three distinct quantities: none of the sparse maps improves validation loss over softmax, yet all of them make the trained model less sensitive than softmax to increasing the inference-time budget.

blocks.en:
Our results also say where a sparse router should be designed, rather than merely swapped in.
Because the router co-adapts its score scale to the map, that scale is a modelling choice that we currently leave to the optimizer, and it would be better learned explicitly, as is already done for sparse attention ( Correia et al., 2019 ; Vasylenko et al., 2026 ) .
A router whose scale is under control could then be trusted to choose its own budget: the sparse maps already assign zero weight to most of the extra slots when K K is raised, so selecting every expert in the support instead of a fixed top- K K , capped by an at-most- k k operator, is a small step from what the trained models already do.
The balancing objective is another design choice to test: its gradients depend on the map, so changing the probabilities used for balancing may alter the score scales and expert loads learned during training.
We leave these directions to future work.

由于路由器将其分数尺度共同调整到地图上,该分数尺度是一个模型选择,我们目前留给优化器来选择,并且它将会被更明确地学习,正如已经对稀有的注意力所做的那样(Correia等,2019;Vasylenko等,2026).
然后可以信任一个其规模处于控制之中的路由器来选择自己的预算:当K K 升起时,稀有的地图已经给大部分的额外插槽分配了零重量,所以选择支持中的每一个专家而不是固定的上--K K K 由最高-k k 的操作员来封顶,是和训练过的模型已经做的一个小步骤.
平衡目标是测试的另一种设计选择:它的梯度取决于地图,因此改变用于平衡的概率可能会改变分数表和在训练中学会的专家负载.
我们把这些方向留给今后的工作。

blocks.en:
Our matched comparison uses a single training seed per configuration, so the small quality differences between maps (at most 0.012 0.012 nats of validation loss) do not establish a ranking.
We test two members of the entmax family ( α = 1.5 \alpha=1.5 and sparsemax, α = 2 \alpha=2 ), one normmax ( γ = 2 \gamma=2 ) and one balancing objective, whose probabilities we vary in a single 300M ablation.
Contributor counts measure expert participation, not compute. As such, whether zero-weight experts are skipped, and what that saves, depends on the dispatch implementation, which we do not measure.
We did not verify that the diagnostic samples are disjoint from the training data.
Finally, the score-scale analysis is descriptive: it relates each router’s singleton rate to its learned gap distribution but does not identify the training mechanism that produced the smaller scales.
blocks.zh:
我们的匹配比较使用每个配置的单一训练种子,因此地图之间的小质量差异(最多为0.0120.012纳特的验证损失)没有建立排名.
我们测试entmax家族的两个成员(α = 1.5\alpha= 1.5和稀有max,α = 2\alpha= 2.),一个规范max(γ = 2\gamma= 2.)和一个平衡目标,其概率我们以单一的300M平面变化来变化.
贡献者衡量专家的参与,而不是计算。 因此,零重量专家是否被忽略,以及这能节省什么,取决于是否及时执行,我们不衡量这一点。
我们没有核实诊断样本是否与培训数据脱节。
最后,分数级分析是描述性的:它把每个路由器的单吨率与其所学到的差距分布联系起来,但没有确定产生较小分数级的培训机制。

The table makes the scale effect visible: at 1B, 7.8 % 7.8\% of the softmax router’s gaps exceed 2 2 and 44.8 % 44.8\% exceed 1 1 , whereas the 1.5 1.5 -entmax router, with an RMS less than half as large, has only 0.05 % 0.05\% of its gaps above 2 2 and 8.3 % 8.3\% above 1 1 .
Sparsemax and normmax-2 sit at the same threshold, so the difference between their singleton rates ( 6.9 % 6.9\% against 21.3 % 21.3\% ) is entirely a difference between the gap distributions their routers learned; Table 7 shows that it comes from the whole distribution being shifted up rather than from a heavier tail, since normmax-2’s median gap is 0.61 0.61 against 0.40 0.40 for sparsemax and its 90 90 th percentile 1.06 1.06 against 0.81 0.81 .
These fractions describe the recorded score distributions in threshold units; they do not apply one router’s map to another router’s scores.
